title: OLED vs LCD: screens that make their own light
examples: What is the difference between OLED and LCD?
Why do OLED screens have perfect blacks?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: OLED wins at deep blacks; LCD is often cheaper and brighter

explain.say: An OLED screen has no backlight. Every red, green and blue subpixel is a tiny light made of organic, carbon-based material that glows when current flows through it.

draw.text: OLED vs LCD: screens that make their own light

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: OLED wins at deep blacks; LCD is often cheaper and brighter

explain.say: An LCD instead filters a backlight that is always on. Its liquid crystal shutters can never block all the light, so even a black pixel leaks a little and looks dark grey.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: OLED wins at deep blacks; LCD is often cheaper and brighter

explain.say: An OLED pixel can switch fully off, giving perfect black and saving power on dark images. Its layers are so thin that a screen can be made flexible, which is how folding phones work.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: OLED wins at deep blacks; LCD is often cheaper and brighter

explain.say: But OLED materials slowly wear as they glow, so a logo shown for months can leave a faint ghost, called burn-in. LCDs avoid that and are often cheaper and brighter, so both are still made.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: OLED wins at deep blacks; LCD is often cheaper and brighter

faq.a: OLED stands for organic light-emitting diode. Organic means the glowing material is made of carbon-based molecules. When current flows, electrons and holes meet in that thin layer and give off light.
asks: How does an OLED pixel make light?

faq.q: How does an LCD screen compare with OLED?
faq.a: An LCD uses a backlight that is always on and liquid crystal shutters to dim each subpixel. It is usually cheaper and can be very bright, but blacks look slightly grey.

faq.q: Why do OLED screens have perfect black?
faq.a: Each OLED subpixel makes its own light, so a black pixel is simply switched off and gives out no light at all. An LCD always has its backlight on behind it.
asks: Why is black so dark on OLED?

faq.a: OLED materials slowly dim the more they glow. If the same bright image, like a logo or keyboard, stays in one place for a very long time, those pixels wear faster and leave a faint ghost image.
asks: Why does my phone have a ghost image?

faq.q: How do folding phone screens bend?
faq.a: An OLED screen has no rigid backlight or thick glass layers. Its glowing layers can be built on a thin flexible plastic and covered with ultra-thin glass, so the whole screen can fold.

facts: OLED stands for organic light-emitting diode.
Practical OLEDs were first reported by Ching Tang and Steven Van Slyke at Kodak in 1987.

quiz.say: Why does an OLED screen show deeper black than an LCD?
quiz.why: OLED pixels make their own light, so a black pixel just turns off.

wrong.1: OLED screens have no backlight at all.
wrong.2: The glass is clear; black comes from pixels being off.
